comma-splice.wrongChoice: Mika was the cashier on duty, she counted the receipts.
comma-splice.mistakeNote: Joins two independent clauses with only a comma.

run-on-or-case.wrongChoice: Mika was the cashier on duty she counted the receipts.
run-on-or-case.mistakeNote: Runs two independent clauses together with no mark or joining word.

however-splice.mistakeNote: Treats however like a coordinating conjunction, so a comma alone seems enough to join the clauses.

modal-meaning.mistakeNote: Uses a possibility modal where the policy states a requirement.

modal-plus-to.mistakeNote: Inserts to after the modal might.

modal-verb-ending.mistakeNote: Adds an -s ending to the verb after a modal.

dangling-opening.wrongChoice: After inspecting the roof, repairs were approved by the engineer.
dangling-opening.mistakeNote: Gives the opening action to repairs instead of the engineer.

parallel-list.mistakeNote: Accepts a to-plus-verb phrase among base verbs in a list.

like-comparison.mistakeNote: Accepts a rating compared with the physical models.

past-time-clue.mistakeNote: Uses an ongoing present form with the past clue yesterday.

participle-after-had.mistakeNote: Accepts a base verb after had.

which-event-gets-had.mistakeNote: Changes the later event instead of the earlier one.

phrase-vs-dependent.mistakeNote: Counts a phrase with no subject and verb as a clause.

count-all-clauses.wrongChoice: Two independent clauses with no dependent clause

who-vs-whom.mistakeNote: Accepts an object form as the subject of a clause.

object-after-preposition.mistakeNote: Uses a subject form after the preposition between.

unclear-pronoun.mistakeNote: Assumes the context shows which of two men the pronoun means.

nearest-noun.mistakeNote: Misses the singular head every one because plural laptops sits near the verb.

mass-noun-some.wrongChoice: Some of the information in these notes are confidential for legal reasons.
mass-noun-some.mistakeNote: Matches the verb to plural notes instead of the mass noun information.

collective-unit.mistakeNote: Marks a singular verb as an error because a panel has several members.

check-opposite-direction.mistakeNote: Picks a similar meaning when the question asks for the opposite.
Picks a word that fits the sentence but is not the opposite.

read-every-word-part.mistakeNote: Reads helpful and ignores the prefix un-.
Focuses on help and loses the negative prefix.
